info.title: nwngram
info.description: nwngram is a CLI application to perform Text Classification on the string of text you provide. Text Classification is a machine learning technique that calculates the similarity between the string of text you need to categorize and a collection of already categorized strings you provide to the library.

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription: Command-line application to perform text classification tasks.

commands.name: session
commands.description: Groups all the features related to a single text classification session.

commands.name: classify
commands.description: Attempt to classify the provided text snippet(s) according to the provided labeled examples.

options.name: --labeledexamples
options.description: The filename of the JSON file containing the labeled examples required to train the classifier. The file needs to be stored in the working folder.

options.name: --textsnippets
options.description: The filename of the JSON file containing the text snippets that the user wants to classify. The file needs to be stored in the working folder.

options.name: --folderpath
options.description: (Optional) The path of the working folder. If not specified, '<path>' will be used.

options.name: --tokenizerruleset
options.description: (Optional) The filename of the JSON file containing the tokenizer ruleset. The file needs to be stored in the working folder. If not specified, default rules will be used.

options.name: --minaccuracysingle
options.description: (Optional) When a single label provided as example, the minimum index average required to return it as classification result. Value can be between 0.0 and 1.0. If not specified, '0.5' will be used.

options.name: --minaccuracymultiple
options.description: (Optional) When multiple labels provided as example, the minimum index average required to return the highest among them as classification result. Value can be between 0.0 and 1.0. If not specified, '0' will be used.

options.name: --savesession
options.description: (Optional) If provided, the text classification session will be saved as JSON in the working folder.

options.name: --cleanlabeledexamples
options.description: (Optional) If provided, any labeled examples that cause the tokenizer to fail will be removed before starting the classification session.

options.name: --disableindexserialization
options.description: (Optional) To use in conjunction with '--savesession'. It has no effect if provided by its own.
